appendix.category: A01 broken access control / MCP tool permission boundary (P-02)
appendix.summary: run_agent_loop honours a caller-supplied agent_name and never calls checkAgentAccess; the backend loop route gates on owner-equivalence and stamps source_agent_name from the agent key. Any holder of an agent-scoped key can start a bounded loop on any same-owner agent without an edge, and the rows violate IA-01's own signal. Same class as the per-endpoint admin gate that took five occurrences (#1890): a per-tool gate is discipline, not a mechanism.
appendix.exploit: 1) obtain agent A's TRINITY_MCP_API_KEY (A is compromised, or an operator can exec into its container); 2) call run_agent_loop(agent_name=B, message=..., max_runs=N) through the MCP server; 3) B runs N iterations of attacker-chosen instructions, spending B's budget, with every row attributed to A.
appendix.disposition: tracked as abilityai/trinity-enterprise#628 (one-line fix at the MCP layer + audit of sibling agent-targeting tools); carried in the harness as a strict xfail worded as the promise
